title: feat: improve economics reconciliation workflow
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Adds secure Google Drive invoice previews for individual transaction documents.
- Opens folders directly for transactions backed by multiple documents and marks missing evidence clearly.
- Defaults the dashboard to the latest closed month so incomplete month-to-date data is not selected automatically.
- Normalizes Vast vendor naming across economics datasets.
- Validated with Biome, the full economics test suite (171 tests), and TypeScript type checking.

gist.headline: Receipts find their flowers
gist.blurb: The economics dashboard now follows transaction evidence more neatly: single invoices open as secure previews, bundles lead straight to their folder, and missing paperwork stops pretending to be invisible.
gist.summary: Improved the internal economics reconciliation dashboard with secure Google Drive previews for single transaction invoices, direct folder links for multi-document transactions, explicit missing-evidence states, latest-closed-month defaults, and normalized Vast vendor names.
gist.impact: Finance operators can reconcile completed months with clearer document trails, while invoice bundles and missing evidence are immediately distinguishable.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy bookkeeping garden: Polli, wearing tiny accountant glasses and a green visor, sorts transaction receipts into labeled flower pots while a CRT monitor robot opens a secure document preview and a folder full of multiple invoices. A calendar flower is set to the latest completed month, and a clearly empty evidence pot is marked with a gentle pixel icon rather than hidden.
gist.image_prompt: Cozy pixel art scene in a warm garden-shed bookkeeping desk where the cute pollinations bee mascot has a tiny green accountant visor and round glasses, sorting invoice papers into lime green (#ecf874) flower pots beside a CRT monitor robot showing a secure document preview; a folder of several receipts sits nearby and one empty pot is clearly marked "MISSING" in simple dark-purple pixel text. Cozy 8-bit pixel art aesthetic, soft pastel gradients, warm lighting, retro gaming vibes like Stardew Valley, code-vines and small flowers around the desk, emotionally warm and gently organized.
